claims.claim: Irenaeus was the bishop of Lugdunum (Lyons) in Gaul during the late second century.
He was born in Asia Minor, probably in Smyrna or a nearby province, sometime between about AD 115 and AD 142.
As a youth he heard and saw the holy bishop Polycarp of Smyrna, giving him a direct link to the apostolic generation.
After the persecution of the Church of Lyons in AD 177, Irenaeus succeeded the martyr Saint Pothinus as bishop of Lyons.
The letter was addressed to Pope Victor I of Rome, the head of the Roman Church.
Its immediate purpose was to protest Victor’s decision to excommunicate the Asian Quartodeciman churches over the date of Easter.
In the same letter Irenaeus warned Victor about the heretical presbyter Florinus, a follower of Valentinian Gnosticism, whose books he called “abominable.”
